findings: The final CNOT ring updates the current bits in order 0→1, 1→2, 2→0, with wire 0 as the most significant bit. Original indices 0 through 7 map to [0, 5, 7, 2, 3, 6, 4, 1]. The resulting sector IDs in final-index order are [0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0], which recover the pre-ring wire-0 partition.

All three presence heads share the same readout factorization. With null logit zero and positive logits g + log_softmax(u), total positive probability is sigmoid(g) and the conditional positive distribution is softmax(u). Identity masses sum squared sector-overlap magnitudes, so a common phase rotation within either sector preserves them. Q presence sums the two overlaps before squaring and can therefore depend on their relative phase.
